item.title: New constraints on holographic dark energy with high-redshift galaxy observations from JWST
item.description: arXiv:2610.35951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Observations of high-redshift galaxies from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) provide a complementary probe of early structure formation. Meanwhile, DESI results have provided further indications of possible dynamical dark energy, prompting investigations of theoretically motivated dark energy models. In this work, we investigate holographic dark energy (HDE) and interacting holographic dark energy (IHDE) using JWST ultraviolet luminosity function measurements, cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations from Planck and ACT, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation measurements, and DES-Dovekie type~Ia supernova data. We find that JWST has little impact on the parameter constraints of $\Lambda$CDM and HDE but produces more pronounced changes in those of IHDE. For CMB+DESI+DES-Dovekie, adding JWST shifts the holographic parameter $c$ from $1.270^{+0.146}_{-0.096}$ to $1.091\pm0.095$ and the interaction parameter $\beta$ from $0.650^{+0.104}_{-0.034}$ to $0.498^{+0.090}_{-0.061}$, accompanied by an increase in $\Omega_{\rm m}$ and a decrease in $S_8$. For the full data combination, $\chi^2_{\rm JWST}$ decreases by approximately $7$ for both HDE and IHDE compared with $\Lambda$CDM, indicating improved fits to the high-redshift galaxy abundances. Our results highlight the complementary role of high-redshift galaxy observations in probing the HDE and IHDE models.
item.dc:creator: Sheng-Han Zhou, Tian-Nuo Li, Guo-Hong Du, Yi-Min Zhang, Yun-He Li, Jing-Fei Zhang, Xin Zhang

item.title: Dynamical systems analysis of Bianchi type-IX cosmology with a scalar field mediated dark sector interaction
item.description: arXiv:2610.35953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recent DESI DR2 results preference for a time-varying dark-energy equation of state, together with the long-standing difficulty of explaining why an initially anisotropic universe should evolve toward isotropy, motivates the study of interacting dark-sector models in anisotropic backgrounds. We investigate the dynamics of Bianchi type-IX cosmologies containing pressureless dark matter coupled to dark energy in the form of a quintessence scalar field $\phi$ with exponential potential $V(\phi)=V_0\,e^{-\lambda\phi}$. Energy exchange between the two dark components is mediated by the scalar field through the interaction term $Q=\kappa\beta\dot\phi\,\rho_{\rm DM}$, where $\kappa^2=8\pi G$ and $\beta$ is a dimensionless coupling. Because Bianchi~IX models generically recollapse, the Hubble scalar $H$ vanishes at the moment of maximum expansion, where the expansion-normalized variables of the standard Wainwright--Ellis formalism diverge. We therefore adopt the $D$-normalized phase-space formalism of Hewitt, Uggla, and Wainwright, which compactifies the state space and remains regular through the recollapse, including the moment of maximum expansion at which $H = 0$. Together with the modified conservation equations for the two dark components, the Einstein equation reduces to a closed autonomous polynomial dynamical system, whose fixed points we classify by linear stability analysis, supplemented by center-manifold theory for the non-hyperbolic points. The fixed points shows the kinetic-dominated, coupling modified matter dominated, curvature scalar, scalar field dominated and coupled scaling families; the last is the anisotropic analogue of the Amendola scaling attractor. Restricting to the initially expanding, isotropizing trajectories, we map the region of the $(\lambda,\beta)$ plane in which anisotropic Bianchi~IX models approach an accelerating Friedmann--Robertson--Walker state.
item.dc:creator: Ashmita, Jaturaporn Watanakampolkij, Daris Samart

item.title: Structure of Logarithmically-Corrected Starobinsky Fuzzy Dark Matter Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.35974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work constructs an anisotropic, Einasto-profile fuzzy dark matter (DM) black hole (BH) using a logarithmically-corrected Starobinsky gravity, $f(R)=R+\beta R^2+\gamma R^2\ln(R/\mu^2)$, a form motivated by one-loop quantum corrections to the gravitational action rather than by the pure quadratic term alone. We derive the generalized trace equation for this action, show that its $\beta$- and $\gamma$-dependence collapses to a single compact source term, and solve the resulting field equations perturbatively about an exact general-relativistic (GR) background for two distinct anisotropic equations of state: a de~Sitter-type branch and a non-local branch, the latter worked through to a closed tangential-pressure profile rather than left incomplete. The logarithmic correction is found to raise the extremal (zero-temperature) threshold relative to pure quadratic gravity and to increase the core tangential pressure noticeably in the non-local branch.
item.dc:creator: M. Ilyas, Fatima Bint-e-Munir, Rana Zaman Ahmad, M. Shahan

item.title: Testing Schouten--Codazzi Gravity: Cosmological Constraints and Deviations from $\Lambda$CDM
item.description: arXiv:2610.36002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schouten--Codazzi gravity (SCG) admits a cosmological background that extends flat $\Lambda$CDM by one integration constant, $\gamma_0$. Its contribution to the Friedmann equation scales as $(1+z)$ and corresponds to an effective component with equation of state $w_{\gamma_0}=-2/3$. We constrain this extension using 15 combinations of Type~Ia supernovae, DESI~DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, and compressed cosmic microwave background information, supplemented by a big-bang nucleosynthesis prior as specified in the analysis. Supernovae paired with either BAO or CMB favor positive $\Omega_{\gamma_0}\equiv\gamma_0/H_0^2$, with approximate marginal departures from zero of $1.7$--$3.2\sigma$. In contrast, all three supernovae$+$BAO$+$CMB combinations are consistent with $\Omega_{\gamma_0}=0$ within their 68\% credible intervals. Their central log Bayes factors favor $\Lambda$CDM, with $\Delta\ln\mathcal{Z}$ between $-2.54$ and $-1.13$, and the inferred Hubble constants remain close to those of the corresponding $\Lambda$CDM fits. These results provide a background-level test of SCG conditional on the adopted priors and likelihood approximations, particularly the model assumptions entering the CMB compression.
item.dc:creator: Andoni Fontanet, Andrea Valencia, Shahnawaz A. Adil, Sebasti\'an N\'ajera, Roberto A. Sussman, J. Alberto V\'azquez, Juan Carlos Hidalgo

item.title: Descartes Curvature Geometry, Compact-Cycle Amplitudes, and the GST Cabibbo Seed
item.description: arXiv:2610.36960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several apparently distinct formulations of the charged-lepton mass relation $p_2/e_1^2 = 2/3$ share a common algebraic object: the ratio of flavor-breaking to flavor-symmetric amplitude components on an internal family space. We show that (i) the relation expressed as a Fourier-mode constraint on Shulga's compact cycle, (ii) the same relation as a Descartes curvature condition in the sense of Kocik, and (iii) the Soddy completion of the resulting circle configuration are related by exact algebra, with no approximations. The Soddy completion defines a companion scale $F^2 = \alpha^2 \mu_\star$ with $\alpha = \sqrt{3/2} - 1$ and $\mu_\star = \sum_\ell m_\ell$; identifying this scale with $\bar{m}^{\rm MS}_s(\mu_\star)$ yields a light-quark mass cascade with the ratio $m_d/m_s = 5/2 - \sqrt{6}$. Combined with the leading Gatto-Sartori-Tonin relation, this gives the down-sector Cabibbo seed $\sqrt{m_d/m_s} = \sqrt{3/2} - 1 = 0.22474\ldots$, numerically close to the measured $|V_{us}| = 0.22503 \pm 0.00068$ ($0.4\sigma$). A full CKM evaluation requires the up-sector phase correction, which we defer. The correspondence is testable by future lattice QCD+QED determinations of $m_d/m_s$; explicit failure modes are listed.
item.dc:creator: Andrew M. Brilliant
